precepts.text: Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. When it says thy neighbour, like we read in Leviticus, it means the children of thy people: your own nation. That's something we have not learned; you look at South Africa and they have not learned it either, despising their own people. God's laws must continue to be pushed and taught in this earth. No one is entering New Jerusalem with hatred in their heart.
precepts.point: The envy also of Ephraim shall depart, and the adversaries of Judah shall be cut off: Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim. Whatever the northern kingdom has against the southern kingdom must depart.

precepts.why:
“Master, which is the great commandment in the law? Jesus said unto him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.”

When it says your neighbour, like we read in Leviticus 19:18, it means “the children of thy people.” That is your race. It is literally saying, love your race.

And that is something we have not learned. Look at South Africa: they have not learned it. They love the white man more than their own brother and sister that look just like them, and they despise their own people.

So God’s laws must continue to be pushed and taught in this earth. Ephraim will stop envying Judah, and Judah will stop vexing Ephraim, only when the tribes keep the second great commandment and love the children of their own people as themselves. No one is entering New Jerusalem with hatred in their heart.

precepts.text: A lawyer, a scribe who copied the law and knew it, tempted Christ with the great commandment: love the Lord with all thy heart, the first four, and love thy neighbour as thyself, the six; on these two hang all the law and the prophets.
precepts.point: Whosoever shall keep the whole law and yet offend in one point is guilty of all: the Christian says you cannot keep them, but the context is the royal law, as the next verse shows, he that said do not commit adultery said also do not kill. Speak and do as they that shall be judged by the law of liberty, since Christ redeemed us from the death the moral law carried; he shall have judgment without mercy that hath showed no mercy.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
“But when the Pharisees had heard that he had put the Sadducees to silence, they were gathered together.” Christ had put the Sadducees to shame, and the Pharisees saw how sharp he was. “Then one of them, which was a lawyer, asked him a question, tempting him.”

A lawyer is a scribe. Their job was writing the Bible over and over again, because ink fades and animal skin and paper rip and smear, so it had to be copied again and again. They were the recorders and copyists, and they knew the law and the prophets off top. That is why he was tempting Christ: he already knew the answer. “Master, which is the great commandment in the law?”

“Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment.” That is the first four of the ten spoken commandments. “And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.” That is the six, the royal law of James 2:8.

“On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.” These two are an abbreviation of all the laws. Loving God with all your heart, soul and mind means keeping the Sabbath day holy, the Passover, Tabernacles, Pentecost, the new moons, keeping the congregation, and the dietary law: don’t drink blood, don’t eat pork or shrimp. That is all serving God. The ten are an umbrella over all of them.

precepts.text: The Sadducees put to Christ the case of seven brethren who under this law took one wife.
precepts.point: The man who refused was called before the elders; his brother's wife loosed his shoe from off his foot, spat in his face, and answered, So shall it be done unto that man that will not build up his brother's house; and his name was called in Israel, The house of him that hath his shoe loosed.

note.label: Deuteronomy 25: Just Judgment, the Brother's Duty, and Amalek

precepts.why:
The Sadducees, which say that there is no resurrection, put this very law to Christ: “Master, Moses said, If a man die, having no children, his brother shall marry his wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.” They gave the case of seven brethren who under this law took one wife, the first dying without issue and leaving his wife unto his brother, “Likewise the second also, and the third, unto the seventh”, and asked whose wife she would be in the resurrection, for they all had her.

“Jesus answered and said unto them, Ye do err, not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of God. For in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels of God in heaven.” The duty of the husband's brother was for a name in Israel and the land inheritance; in the resurrection there is no marrying at all.

precepts.text: For unto me the children of Israel are servants; they are my servants whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt.
precepts.point: The servants in this parable are not any man who says he loves God. The scripture names who the servants are.

note.label: Matthew 22: The Marriage of the King's Son and the Great Commandment

precepts.why:
In the parable a certain king made a marriage for his son and “sent forth his servants to call them that were bidden to the wedding”. The servants are not any man who says he loves God. The scripture names who the servants are: “For unto me the children of Israel are servants; they are my servants whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt: I am the Lord your God.”

The children of Israel are the Most High's servants because he brought them out of the land of Egypt. So the servants the king sent forth to call the bidden, and the other servants he sent again saying “all things are ready: come unto the marriage”, are Israel. They are the ones sent with the call to the wedding, and the ones the remnant “took” and “entreated them spitefully, and slew”.

precepts.text: Let thy priests be clothed with righteousness; and let thy saints shout for joy.
precepts.point: The garment is not cloth. It is righteousness, which is the keeping of the laws of the Most High.

note.label: Matthew 22: The Marriage of the King's Son and the Great Commandment

precepts.why:
The king found a man “which had not on a wedding garment”, and when asked how he came in without one, “he was speechless.” He was bound hand and foot and cast into outer darkness, “there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth. For many are called, but few are chosen.”

The garment is not cloth. David shows what it is: “Let thy priests be clothed with righteousness; and let thy saints shout for joy.” Righteousness is the clothing, and righteousness is the keeping of the laws of the Most High.

So the man without the wedding garment is one who came to the marriage without righteousness, without keeping the laws. That is why he had no answer for the king, and why many are called but few are chosen.

precepts.text: The law they were standing on: her husband's brother shall go in unto her, and perform the duty of an husband's brother unto her.
precepts.point: This is not saying there is no marriage in the kingdom. It answers the law they built the question on, which will not need to be kept when there is no more dying.

note.label: Matthew 22: The Marriage of the King's Son and the Great Commandment

precepts.why:
The Sadducees, “which say that there is no resurrection”, built their question on this law: “If brethren dwell together, and one of them die, and have no child, the wife of the dead shall not marry without unto a stranger: her husband’s brother shall go in unto her, and take her to him to wife, and perform the duty of an husband’s brother unto her.”

That is the law they were standing on when they said, “Moses said, If a man die, having no children, his brother shall marry his wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.” They stacked up seven brethren and one wife to make the resurrection look absurd: “whose wife shall she be of the seven?”

Christ answered, “Ye do err, not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of God.” In the resurrection “they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels of God in heaven.” That is not saying there is no marriage in the kingdom. It answers the law of the husband's brother, a law given because men die and leave no child. When there is no more dying, that law will not need to be kept, and the Sadducees' riddle falls apart.

precepts.text: The Sadducees try to confound Christ with the woman who had seven husbands, asking whose wife she will be in the resurrection, and he answers that in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels.
precepts.point: The Sadducees did not even believe in the resurrection, yet they used scriptures they did not believe to try to confound Christ, the same way Christians and five-percenters take our scriptures they reject and use them to try to confound us.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

precepts.why:
“The same day came to him the Sadducees, which say that there is no resurrection”, and they used a scripture they did not believe to try to confound Christ: Moses said a man's brother must marry his wife and raise up seed, so with seven brethren who all had her, “in the resurrection whose wife shall she be of the seven?”

Christ answered, “Ye do err, not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of God. For in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels of God in heaven.”

That is the same thing Christians and five-percenters do: take our scriptures that they reject and use them to try to confound us. And it is the same reason these pastors avoid a real sit-down with someone who actually knows the scriptures.

God sent forth Rome against us; that’s his armies. “But they which were bidden were not worthy.” “Both bad and good”: bad Israelites and good Israelites came in. “He saw there a man which had not on a wedding garment”: remember the garment represents the righteousness, which is the keeping of the commandments. This dude was naked, meaning he was in the midst of sin. “And he was speechless”: he didn’t know what to say. “And cast him into outer darkness”: that’s destruction; kill him. “For many are called, but few are chosen.”
